Data


Show code
library(tidyverse)

products <- read_csv("data/olist_products_dataset.csv")
orders <- read_csv("data/olist_orders_dataset.csv")
reviews <- read_csv("data/olist_order_reviews_dataset.csv")
order_items <- read_csv("data/olist_order_items_dataset.csv")

analysis_data <- order_items%>%
  left_join(products, by = "product_id") %>%
  left_join(orders, by = "order_id") %>%
  left_join(reviews, by = "order_id")


Data: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/olistbr/brazilian-ecommerce/code Observation Unit: Individual product listing Dimension: 113314 x 28 Response: Total sales volume Candidate Predictors: Average Product rating score, Total review count, Listed price and Product category Evidence: Having both customer feedback metrics like ratings/reviews and commercial metrics like price and sales allows us to model the preditive relationship. Permission: It is a data set offered on a public website called Kaggle.

text:
One useful first look


Show code
# Create one figure that directly informs your research question.
# Include a useful title, labels, units, and accessible colors.

product_summary <- order_items%>%
  group_by(product_id) %>%
  summarize(
    total_sales = n(),
    mean_price = mean(price)
  ) %>%
  left_join(products, by = "product_id")

ggplot(product_summary, aes(x= mean_price, y = total_sales)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, color = "#2b5c8f") +
  labs(
    title = "E- comeerce Sales Volume vs. Product Price",
    subtitle = "Aggregated by product SKU",
    x = "Mean Product Price (BRL)",
    y = "Total Sales Volume"
  )+
    theme_minimal()









This data looks exponential rather than linear. This can cause problems when we run our test. A log transformation is most likely needed to fit the models better.

title: Pricing the market: Predicting E-commerce sales volume using product ratings and price point
text:
Baseline model


Show code
# Fit the baseline and display only the output needed below.
baseline_model <- lm(total_sales ~ mean_price, data = product_summary)
summary(baseline_model)



Call:
lm(formula = total_sales ~ mean_price, data = product_summary)

Residuals:

Multiple R-squared:  0.001033,  Adjusted R-squared:  0.001003 
F-statistic: 34.07 on 1 and 32949 DF,  p-value: 5.365e-09


Mean price has a negative direction. For every 1 brazillian real increase is a product’s mean price, we expect its total sales volume to decrease by 0.0014 unit holding all else constant. The p-value is low so we’ll reject the null hypothesis and conclude that mean rpice has a significant effect on total sales. The one limiation that we have is that the data follows an exponential decay shape so a linear regrssion isn’t the best fit unless there is some log transformaton include.

Proposed extension
We plan to extend our baseline model by adding average product rating, review count, and product category as predictors of product sales volume. We will also investigate whether a log transformation improves the model.

Check model diagnostics, including residual plots, to assess linearity and constant variance. Compare the baseline and extended models and verify that our written conclusions match the R output.
